Q5828165.label: 1964 Mexican general election
Q5828165.summary: General elections were held in Mexico on 5 July 1964. The presidential elections were won by Gustavo Díaz Ordaz, who received 89% of the vote. In the Chamber of Deputies election, the Institutional Revolutionary Party won 175 of the 210 seats.

Q3586629.label: 1991 Portuguese presidential election
Q3586629.summary: A presidential election was held in Portugal on 13 January 1991.

Q23132741.label: 2019 Polish parliamentary election
Q23132741.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Poland on 13 October 2019. All 460 members of the Sejm and 100 senators of the Senate were elected. The ruling right-wing Law and Justice (PiS) won re-election to a second term retaining its majority in the Sejm. However, it lost its majority in the Senate to the opposition.

Q1791557.label: 1976 Italian general election
Q1791557.summary: The 1976 Italian general election was held in Italy on 20 June 1976. It was the first election after the voting age was lowered to 18.

Q3722309.label: 1958 Albanian parliamentary election
Q3722309.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in the People's Republic of Albania on 1 June 1958. The Democratic Front, dominated by the Communist Party of Labour of Albania, was the only organization able to contest the elections, and subsequently won all 188 seats. Voter turnout was reported to be almost 100%.

Q6433349.label: 2011 Kosovan presidential election
Q6433349.summary: Indirect presidential elections were held in Kosovo on 22 February 2011 and 7 April 2011.

Q7541829.label: Slovenian RTVS referendum, 2005
Q7541829.summary: A referendum on political control of Radiotelevizija Slovenija was held in Slovenia on 25 September 2005. Voters were asked whether they approved of increasing political control of the country's public broadcaster. The proposal was approved by 50.7% of voters, although voter turnout was only 30.7%.

Q5985861.label: 1944 Icelandic presidential election
Q5985861.summary: Indirect presidential elections were held in Iceland on 17 June 1944 following the approval of a new constitution and the transition of the country to a republic the previous month. Sveinn Björnsson was elected and appointed by the Parliament for a one-year term.

Q269893.label: 2010 Moscow Metro bombings
Q269893.desc: 2010 terrorist attack by Islamist militants in Moscow
Q269893.summary: The 2010 Moscow Metro bombings were suicide bombings carried out by two female Islamic terrorists during the morning rush hour of March 29, 2010, at two stations of the Moscow Metro, with roughly 40 minutes in between. At least 40 people were killed, and over 100 injured.

mentions.c: Russia: Terrorist attack: 2010 Moscow Metro bombings

Q2888261.label: Battle of Cañada Strongest
Q2888261.summary: The Battle of Cañada Strongest was a major military action from May 10 to May 25, 1934 during the Chaco War, in which Paraguayan forces were ambushed and defeated by three Bolivian divisions. The engagement is considered the greatest victory of the Bolivian army during the war.

Q2526789.label: Battle of Zeeland
Q2526789.img: Een Duitse mitrailleurploeg bij de prikkeldraadversperring van de Zanddijkstelling.jpg
Q2526789.summary: The Battle of Zeeland occurred on the Western Front during the early stages of the German assault on France and the Low Countries during World War II. Several Dutch and French units attempted to hold off the German onslaught by making a determined defense of the Dutch province of Zeeland. The battle lasted eight days and was a defeat for the French and Dutch forces defending the province.

Q2280517.label: Battle of San Marino
Q2280517.summary: The Battle of San Marino was an engagement on 17–20 September 1944 during the Italian Campaign of the Second World War, in which German Army forces occupied the neutral Republic of San Marino microstate and were then attacked by Allied forces. It is also sometimes known as the Battle of Monte Pulito.

Q4871237.label: Battle of Hoa Binh
Q4871237.desc: 1951 battle of the First Indochina War
Q4871237.summary: The Battle of Hòa Bình was fought during the First Indochina War. It occurred from 10 November 1951 to 25 February 1952, when French Union forces attempted to lure the Việt Minh out into the open and to force it to fight on French terms.

Q2026053.label: Operation Dragon Strike
Q2026053.desc: NATO counter-insurgent mission in Kandahar province, Afghanistan
Q2026053.summary: Operation Dragon Strike was a NATO counter-insurgent mission in Kandahar province, Afghanistan, against Taliban forces, which started on September 15, 2010.

Q124795461.desc: Murder of a seven-year-old Palestinian girl and her entire family by Israeli bombing

Q7210053.label: Polish nationalism
Q7210053.desc: Nationalist ideology and movement promoting Poland and the Polish nation
Q7210053.summary: Polish nationalism is a nationalism which asserts that the Polish people are a nation and which affirms the cultural unity of Poles. British historian of Poland Norman Davies defines nationalism as "a doctrine ... to create a nation by arousing people's awareness of their nationality, and to mobilize their feelings into a vehicle for political action."

Q76357.label: Jürgen Habermas
Q76357.summary: Jürgen Habermas was a German philosopher and social theorist in the tradition of critical theory and pragmatism. His work addressed communicative rationality and the public sphere. He held professorships at Heidelberg University and Goethe University Frankfurt and directed the Max Planck Institute in Starnberg.
